description: Glob matching cases for checksync's Rust glob matcher. The expected results come from git 2.56's glob matcher, run as a black box, not from checksync's TypeScript, which doesn't use this matcher.

vectors.description: Literal text must match the whole text
A question mark matches exactly one byte
A star matches any run of bytes, including none
A backslash makes the next byte literal
A backslash at the end of the pattern matches nothing
A bracket set matches one byte from the set
A leading ! or ^ negates a bracket set
A ] straight after the opening bracket or its negation is literal
A dash is literal at the end of a set or after a range
A backslash inside a bracket set escapes the next byte
A backwards range matches only its first byte
A malformed bracket set matches nothing
POSIX classes match their bytes
Only space, tab, line feed and carriage return are spaces
A class starts only where the first ] after [: follows a colon
An unknown class name matches nothing, even in a negated set
A class can't start or end a range
Case folding applies to ASCII letters only
Case folding compares escaped bytes with the text lowercased
Case folding compares bracket bytes with the text lowercased, but ranges and classes also by uppercase
With pathname, ?, * and bracket sets don't match a slash
**/ at the start matches any number of folders, including none
/**/ in the middle matches any number of folders, including none
/** at the end matches everything inside
Three or more stars making up a folder name act as two
Two stars joined to other bytes act as one
** followed by an escaped slash matches across folders, leaving the slash
A slash before ** counts even when escaped
** followed by anything else acts as one star
A NUL byte ends the pattern or the text
Braces and other bytes match themselves
